entries.grounds: sort_keys=False writes the keys in insertion order (init: the example's authoring order; seal: `B.dump`'s fixed order, facts/stories in criteria/story order; approve and continue keep the order of the file they read). Re-run at 289885e on both shipped examples: digest, plan_hash, lint stdout, explain stdout identical; parsed bundle equal; init's authoring.json differs only in key order (both examples have alphabetical story ids S1 / S1,S2,S3, and seal iterates `authoring['stories']` in file order, bundle_cli.py:213, so the plan is the same). The one data-dependent difference I could construct: calc-3's criteria renamed so their authoring order is not alphabetical -> lint's `coverage.requirements[R].criteria` list is in authoring order under the mutant (['C90-C-ADD', ..., 'C86-C-ADD-3']) and sorted under the original (the same set, same verdict NOT_READY, same digest); `coverage` appends criteria in facts order (bundle_cli.py:318-327, 345-347) whereas the sibling lists `criteria_without_*` are sorted (L358-359). That is a report-only list order. Everything the kernel hashes is order-free: `freeze` sorts mapping keys (product/contract.py:32-44, :37) so a contract's nested stimulus/observable arrive sorted whatever the file; canonical/digest sort_keys (contract.py:60-65; bundle.py:139-140); Project.order() sorts (bundle.py:124-136) and the run iterates it (run.py:456) and looks stories/facts up by key (run.py:462,173; feedback.py:82; review_verify.py:202-208).

entries.grounds: Proof from the code, unchanged since P2: Plan.__post_init__ (aisef2/plan/obligation.py:89-102) takes `tuple(self.obligations)` for a list or a tuple (:93), refuses an empty one or a non-PlanObligation (:94-95), REPLACES the field by the tuple (`object.__setattr__`, :96) and only then computes or compares plan_hash (:99-102). So `obligations=list(...)` and `tuple(...)` give the same frozen Plan: same field type, ==, plan_hash, plain(). `require_str_fields` (obligation.py:90; product/contract.py:172-176) reads only fields annotated exactly `str` (id, baseline; skip plan_hash); `obligations` is `tuple[PlanObligation, ...]`. In continue_from the local list `obligations` (L457-465) is not named after L466 and `new_plan` is read only by `plain(new_plan)` (L473). Differential at 289885e on T00a's two-story calc run (fake client): the whole continuation bundle and the whole report of the null mutant and of the mutant are deep-equal (no differing path).
